facts.detail: The January 2026 OMR UPRN-level user guide was published on 4 June 2026 for England and Wales.
Region and local-authority derivation uses the December 2025 National Statistics UPRN Lookup.
Fallback postcode geography uses the November 2025 National Statistics Postcode Lookup.
The release also uses the November 2025 ONS UPRN Directory.
BDUK plans updated releases alongside the latest OMR closure notice once every four months.

facts.detail: The release provides BDUK's current view of Open Market Review determinations.
It includes BDUK's current view of whether a premises has a gigabit connection.
It includes future plans for gigabit-capable connections.
It includes BDUK plans for premises believed not commercially viable.
It is not a comprehensive historical record of GIS, voucher, Gigahub and Superfast delivery.

facts.detail: BDUK says the release is optimised for technical users and is easiest to analyse with programming software.
The guide warns spreadsheet software such as Excel may not display all rows.
The data is released as CSV and comma-containing fields are escaped with quotation marks.
The England and Wales release is split into 318 files by local-authority district.
A sample file containing at most 1,000 rows is provided.

facts.detail: The premises base uses the latest AddressBase Premium epoch available at the OMR.
The base is filtered to remove non-postal addresses and demolished premises.
The UPRN field is a numeric identifier of up to 12 digits for a Great Britain spatial address.
The struprn field prefixes the UPRN with 'str' to help software preserve identifier integrity.
A missing UPRN may reflect demolition, dereliction or a new build absent from the AddressBase epoch.
